draft.title: How infectious diseases spread
card: A pathogen has to get from one host to another. The path it takes is called its route of spread.
droplets or tiny particles from a cough or sneeze are breathed in. Influenza and COVID-19 can spread this way.
a pathogen passes by contact with an infected person or a surface they have touched. Many colds spread this way.
food or water with pathogens in it can cause infection. Animals such as mosquitoes can carry a pathogen from one person to another when they bite.
draft.remember: Find the route a pathogen takes, then block that route to stop the spread.

a.q: Which example shows a disease spreading through animals?
opts: A mosquito bites a sick person, then bites someone else
A student sneezes and a classmate breathes in the droplets
A person eats a salad washed in water with pathogens in it
A child touches a door handle and then rubs their eyes
a.why: A mosquito carries the pathogen from one person to another when it bites. The sneeze is spread through the air, which is a different route even though it also passes between people.
a.clue: Look for a living creature that carries the pathogen between people.

b.q: Many people at a camp in Bendigo become ill after drinking from a tank that was contaminated with pathogens. Which route of spread is this?
b.why: The pathogens reached people through the water they drank, so the route is food and water. Touch is tempting because the people shared one tank, but they were not infected by contact with each other. Closing the tank or treating the water would block this route.
b.clue: What did people take into their bodies?

a.best: A mosquito bites a sick person, then bites someone else
